correctness.rationale: The false-twin lower bound forces every resolving set to contain at least \(q-1\) of the \(q\) brush leaves. A set of exactly those \(q-1\) leaves fails because the omitted brush leaf and \(p_1\) have the same multiset representation, so the dimension is at least \(q\). All \(q\) brush leaves resolve the handle because \(p_i\) has representation \(\{(i+1)^q\}\). For a size-\(q\) basis containing exactly \(q-1\) brush leaves, the added vertex cannot be \(p_0\), while every \(p_j\), \(1\le j\le\ell\), works: a handle representation contains a value of multiplicity at least \(q-1\ge2\), whereas the omitted leaf has only the repeated value \(2\), and the only possible handle collision at \(p_1\) would require \(j+1=|j-1|\), impossible. This proves both the dimension and the complete basis list. The assigned verifier exhausts the stated small box, and a fresh independent brute-force reconstruction for \(2\le\ell\le4\), \(3\le q\le5\) reproduced dimension \(q\) and exactly \(1+q\ell\) bases.
residual_risks: The classification is restricted to brooms with at least three brush leaves.
